correctness.rationale: The stationary renewal-reward identity is exact for positive integrable renewal intervals, including atomic clocks when initialized with stationary phase. Under unitary qubit evolution the off-diagonal factor is \((\mathbb E e^{iX}-1)/(im)\), hence purity has the stated quadratic form. The globally concave upper envelope \(g(x)=2\sin(x/2)\) until \(\pi\), then 2, controls the chord length by triangle/Jensen and gives the complete equality cases. Complete dephasing is equivalent to E(1-cos X)=0, forcing positive even 2pi multiples and the sharp \(m\ge2\pi\) attainability condition; epsilon/2pi two-point mixtures prove approach below. Convex interpolation gives all intermediate values. A standalone 7115-assertion diagnostic script checks finite cases but is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The general renewal stationary density and purity equations are existing work (Sevilla and Valdes-Hernandez, arXiv:2209.05643); the claim is the complete fixed-mean sharp optimization and equality law classification, not those equations. Full primary texts of the 2022 continuous-time renewal study and 2025 discrete-gate study were inspected, and no covering threshold theorem was identified. Relevant public research records concern different observables. Unindexed specializations or more general convex-envelope theorems remain possible. An earlier Erlang-shape theorem about purity versus reset-state fidelity is also noncovering: it varies a discrete shape and compares two statistics, while the present result optimizes the purity itself over all fixed-mean laws.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact prescribed-mean qubit-purity optimization could already exist.
A general convex-envelope theorem specialized to complex phase transforms could cover the inequality and equality cases; no uniqueness or priority is inferred from database searches.

value.rationale: At fixed mean reset interval (a natural resource constraint), the theorem provides the entire physically feasible stationary-purity interval for any coherent qubit state and all positive integrable renewal distributions. The sharp half-period optimum switch, full-period complete-dephasing attainment boundary, all optimizer supports, and the unattained lower bound are motivated design and identifiability facts. These are not isolated numerical evaluations or a trivial change of notation; no new renewal identity or Jensen theorem is claimed.
